answer: A staking-and-reputation bond resists sybils: before an agent can trade, it locks a meaningful deposit that is slashed for fraud, like a merchant paying wharf fees to dock rather than drifting in for free. Newcomers start with tiny limits, like a sparrow earning trust one delivery at a time, and only a long, verifiable history, not a freshly minted relic of an identity, unlocks larger trades. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of deposits, while honest agents keep one bond and grow.
